subject: MedSecure: data residency & isolation blockers — Dedicated vs Private VPC follow-up
content:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@medsecure.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: MedSecure kickoff: deployment/residency recap + open items

Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we promised to follow up on: 

- Customer context: MedSecure needs to process PHI-derived PII from clinical intake forms. Primary requirement is strict logical separation of MedSecure data from other customers and an auditable keystore model.
- Options discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPU pools), Private VPC with customer-managed control plane (highest isolation).

Open items / what you asked us to confirm:
1) Can Dedicated meet MedSecure’s requirement that no other tenant can access customer data (including logs, KV caches, temp storage)?
2) For Private VPC: what level of operational evidence (network diagrams, SOC2 scoping, KMS integration notes) can we provide and what timeline?
3) Any onboarding lead time differences between Dedicated and Private VPC (capacity, IAM setup, contractual ops)?

Next steps (proposed):
- I will share a short ops checklist for Private VPC and a Dedicated-capacity isolation matrix (what we lock down and what requires customer network controls).
- Marissa will attach the mutual action plan and suggested PoC duration.
- Laura will pull the control-plane/KMS notes we can share with your security team.

Thanks — available if you want to jump back on a 20-min follow-up next week.

—Karthik

Thanks Karthik — useful recap. A few clarifying questions from our security team: 

1) Dedicated: you mentioned "no other tenant access" — can you confirm how logs, ephemeral storage, and KV cache are segregated? Are there any shared control-plane components that could see metadata about requests?

2) Encryption: for Private VPC, can we bring our own KMS (Azure Key Vault is our preference)? If so, do you have a documented flow for envelope keys and rotation?

3) Evidence: we need network diagrams and the minimal set of artifacts to run risk assessment (preferably within 5 business days). What can you share without an NDA amendment?

We'd like to keep Hosted API on the table for early non-prod testing, but production will need either Dedicated or Private VPC given the regulatory needs.

—Sam

Sam — looping back with concrete artifacts attached that should help your assessment. Summary below and attachments are the detailed stubs we typically share during an initial risk review.

What Dedicated provides (short):
- Isolated GPU pools: compute hosts are reserved to the account; no inference workloads from other customers are scheduled on those hosts.
- Data plane isolation: model weights and token streams are stored on attached volumes that are provisioned per-account. Ephemeral caches are in-memory by default; where disk-backed caches are used we provision per-account storage.
- Control plane metadata: feature flags and routing decisions are handled by our central orchestration; we provide role-restricted views and can redact request-level metadata from any UI exports. Control plane still exists as a Redwood-managed service — we can discuss SOC-scoped access/log-forwarding.

What Private VPC provides (short):
- Control plane residency options: customer can opt for a private control plane that runs in your VPC (customer-managed or Redwood-managed private control plane), removing Redwood-managed control plane access to per-request metadata.
- KMS: BYOK supported (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, or on-prem HSM). We support envelope encryption with rotation hooks; attached doc has the sequence diagram.
- Network: we provide an infrastructure BOM and sample network ACLs; customer-owned transit and peering options available.

Evidence and timeline:
- Attached: redwood_private_vpc_ops_checklist.pdf (ops checklist, network diagram stub), medsecure_network_requirements_v2.png (sample topology), MAP-MedSecure-20261218.pdf (proposed mutual action plan + PoC scope).
- NDA note: we can share standard SOC2 scope statements and network diagrams under our standard NDA. If you need deeper artifacts (control-plane logs, SOC artifacts), we'll need an evidence-sharing addendum (I can route to legal).
- Timeline: Dedicated ramp (capacity + onboarding) typically 2-3 weeks once contract signed. Private VPC (customer-managed control plane) is 6-8 weeks for full production fit (includes network, KMS integration, and validation). We can support an early non-prod on Hosted API or Dedicated for testing during that period.

Suggested next step: schedule a 30-min security sync with Laura and our security engineer (we've copied her on this thread). Laura — can you share the KMS integration sequence diagram and a short note about what control-plane metadata we can redact/export?

—Marissa
